# package sunspec

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-sunspec"
```

Package sunspec reads, writes and serves SunSpec devices over Modbus.

It discovers SunSpec model chains, decodes standard point types, resolves scale factors, and decodes nested and repeating groups. In the other direction it encodes point values into a model's registers, writes a device's read-write points (Device.WritePoint) and serves a device built from such models. Schemas for standard models are compiled into package registry.

#### Scope {#hdr-Scope}

This package is a domain layer on top of [github.com/otfabric/go-modbus](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-modbus). Transport, retries, logging, metrics, and connection lifecycle belong to the injected \*modbus.Client (which Detect, Discover and Device ask to read registers, function codes 03 and 04, and only Device.WritePoint to write, function code 16), and on the serving side to the \*modbus.Server a Server is handed to. This package does not open or close connections; the one exception is the convenience Server.Serve, which runs a modbus.Server for the duration of a context.

#### Entry points {#hdr-Entry_points}

  - Detect — probe for a SunSpec marker
  - Discover / Open — enumerate models and return a Device
  - Device.ReadAll / ReadModel / ReadModelByID / ReadPoint — read and decode
  - Device.ReadModels — read several models, adjacent ones sharing requests
  - Device.ModelByID / ModelsByID — find model instances by ID
  - Device.WritePoint — write one read-write point (FC 16) and read it back
  - DecodeModel — decode a register slice against a schema (no I/O)
  - EncodeModel — build a model's registers from values by point name (no I/O)
  - NewServer — lay out a device from models and values; the Server is a go-modbus RequestHandler, and its SetPoint / Update methods change values while it is served
  - ReadFunctionCodes — the function codes of a client that cannot write (WritePoint then fails)

Package devicefile reads and writes a device as a JSON file: what a Server is built from, and what a Device that was read can be written as.

#### Ownership {#hdr-Ownership}

The caller creates, opens, and closes the \*modbus.Client. Device holds a reference to that client and does not take ownership. Closing the client invalidates further Device operations.

A Server owns its register map and nothing else. The caller creates, starts and stops the \*modbus.Server that serves it.

#### Concurrency {#hdr-Concurrency}

Device methods are safe for concurrent use to the same extent as the underlying \*modbus.Client. Server methods are safe for concurrent use with each other and with the requests being served. The compiled registry is safe for concurrent reads after package init; callers must not call registry.Register after init.

#### Errors {#hdr-Errors}

See ERRORS.md for sentinels, typed errors, and relationship to Modbus errors.

```go
	// ErrModelLayout indicates models that cannot be laid out or kept in a
```

```go
var ErrPointNotWritable = errors.New("sunspec: point not writable")
```

ErrPointNotWritable indicates a write the client refuses before sending anything: a point whose schema access is not "RW", the count point of a group (it defines the layout), a point of a model without a schema or whose device holds more registers than the schema describes, or a device served in input registers, which Modbus cannot write.

## Functions

### func EncodeModel

```go
func EncodeModel(meta *registry.ModelMeta, values *Values) ([]uint16, error)
```

EncodeModel builds the registers of one model from its schema and values. It is the inverse of DecodeModel and performs no I/O.

The result holds the whole model starting at its header: index 0 is the ID register (meta.ID), index 1 the length register (the number of registers that follow it), then the data in the order of the schema's group tree. Passing it to DecodeModel with the same schema yields the given values. The ID and length registers are set by the encoder and cannot be given.

How values are given, scaled, rounded and checked, and how many instances of a nested group are encoded, is described on Values. A nil values encodes a model in which every point is not implemented.

EncodeModel returns a \*EncodeError, matching ErrEncode, that names the group instance and point at fault. It additionally matches ErrValueOutOfRange for a value that does not fit its point and ErrPointNotFound for a name in Values.Points that the schema's group does not have.

### func ReadFunctionCodes

```go
func ReadFunctionCodes() []modbus.FunctionCode
```

ReadFunctionCodes returns the Modbus function codes the client side of this package sends: Read Holding Registers (0x03) and Read Input Registers (0x04). Detect, Discover, Open and every Device method read registers and do nothing else.

Give the list to modbus.Config.AllowedFunctionCodes (go-modbus v1.5.0 or later) for a client that cannot write: the client then refuses any other function code with modbus.ErrFunctionCodeNotAllowed before a byte is sent, whoever asks for it.

	client, err := modbus.New(modbus.Config{
		URL:                  "tcp://192.168.1.100:502",
		AllowedFunctionCodes: sunspec.ReadFunctionCodes(),
	})

Each call returns a new slice.

### type DecodedGroup

```go
type DecodedGroup struct {
	// Name is the group name from the schema, for example "Crv" or "Pt".
	// For the top-level group it is the model's name.
	Name string
	// Index is the 1-based number of this instance among the instances of the
	// same group within its parent. It is 0 for the top-level group.
	Index int
	// Points holds the group's own decoded points in schema order.
	Points []DecodedPoint
	// Groups holds the instances of the nested groups in register order:
	// all instances of the first nested group, then all of the second, and
	// so on. It is nil for a group without nested instances.
	Groups []*DecodedGroup
}
```

DecodedGroup holds one decoded instance of a group: its own points and the instances of the groups nested inside it.

A simple model has one top-level group and nothing else. A model with a repeating part (the phases of a meter, the trackers of an MPPT extension, the strings of a battery) has one nested instance per repetition in Groups. Curve models nest further: each curve instance holds its point instances.

FindPoint returns the first point with the given name in the group or, depth first in register order, in the groups nested inside it. It returns nil when there is none.

GroupsNamed returns the nested instances with the given group name, in order. Deeper levels are not searched.

#### func (DecodedGroup) Walk


### type DecodedModel

```go
type DecodedModel struct {
	// ModelID is the SunSpec model ID.
	ModelID uint16
	// Name is the schema label (or name), or "unknown_<ID>" for a model
	// without a schema.
	Name string
	// InstanceAddress is the register address of the model header (the ID
	// register) on the device.
	InstanceAddress uint16
	// Schema is the schema the model was decoded with. It is nil when the
	// model was not decoded (no schema, or the read failed). It is shared
	// with the registry and must not be modified.
	Schema *registry.ModelMeta
	// Group is the decoded top-level group: the model's own points and,
	// nested inside it, the instances of its groups. It is nil when the model
	// was not decoded (no schema, the read failed, or too few registers).
	Group *DecodedGroup
	// RawRegisters holds the registers the model was decoded from. For a
	// decoded model this includes the ID and L header registers at index 0
	// and 1; for a model without a schema, or one whose read failed, it holds
	// only the data registers that were read.
	RawRegisters []uint16
	// Warnings holds human-readable notes about anything that could not be
	// read or decoded. A model can carry warnings without an error.
	Warnings []string
}
```

DecodedModel holds the decoded output of a single model instance.

#### func DecodeModel

```go
func DecodeModel(regs []uint16, meta *registry.ModelMeta, instanceAddr uint16) (*DecodedModel, error)
```

DecodeModel decodes a register slice into a DecodedModel using the given schema. It performs no I/O.

regs must hold the whole model starting at its header: regs\[0] is the ID register, regs\[1] the length register, and the data follows. The registers are consumed in the order of the schema's group tree: the top-level group's own points, then every instance of each nested group, depth first. How often a nested group occurs comes from the schema: a fixed count, the value of a count point decoded earlier, or as many instances as the remaining registers hold. instanceAddr is only copied to DecodedModel.InstanceAddress.

The returned model's RawRegisters aliases regs; it is not copied. Problems that leave the rest of the model usable (an unsupported point type, a group that does not fit in the registers, registers left over at the end) are reported in Warnings, not as an error.

DecodeModel returns a \*DecodeError (matching ErrDecode) when meta is nil or has no group, in which case the model is nil too, or when regs is shorter than the top-level group's own points, in which case the returned model holds only the raw registers and a warning.

#### func (DecodedModel) Point

```go
func (m *DecodedModel) Point(name string) *DecodedPoint
```

Point returns the first point with the given name in the model: in the top-level group or, failing that, in the nested groups in register order. It returns nil when the model was not decoded or has no such point.

#### func (DecodedModel) Values

```go
func (m *DecodedModel) Values() *Values
```

Values returns the model's decoded values in the form EncodeModel takes, so that EncodeModel(m.Schema, m.Values()) rebuilds a model that decodes to the same values. It returns nil for a model that was not decoded (Group is nil).

Points the device reports as not implemented are left out, as are the ID and length registers and pad points holding the pad value. A point whose scale factor was resolved to a non-zero exponent is given as its engineering value (ScaledValue); every other point as its RawValue. Enum and bitfield points are given as numbers, not symbol names, so that values the schema does not name survive. Should an engineering value not convert back to the registers it was decoded from (a 64-bit value beyond the precision of a float64, an absurd scale factor, a string of only spaces), the point's registers are given instead, as a \[]uint16.

Every decoded group instance is kept, also one without implemented points, and count points keep their value, so the model's length is preserved. A count point the device reports as not implemented is given as its registers, because leaving it out would encode it as a count of zero.

For a model that decoded without warnings, decoding the result of EncodeModel(m.Schema, m.Values()) yields the same points as m holds.

### type DecodedPoint

```go
type DecodedPoint struct {
	// Name is the point name from the schema, for example "W".
	Name string
	// Type is the SunSpec point type from the schema, for example "int16",
	// "acc32", "enum16", "sunssf" or "string".
	Type string
	// RawValue is the unscaled value. Its dynamic type follows Type: int16
	// (int16, sunssf), uint16 (uint16, count, acc16, enum16, bitfield16,
	// pad), int32, uint32 (uint32, acc32, enum32, bitfield32), int64, uint64
	// (uint64, acc64, bitfield64), float32, float64, string (string, ipaddr,
	// ipv6addr, eui48), or []uint16 holding a copy of the raw registers for
	// an unsupported type or a point with too few registers.
	RawValue any
	// ScaledValue is RawValue multiplied by 10^SFRawValue. It is nil when the
	// point has no scale factor, is not implemented, is not numeric, or its
	// scale factor could not be resolved.
	ScaledValue *float64
	// Units is the unit from the schema (for example "W" or "Hz"), or empty.
	Units string
	// SFName is the scale factor reference from the schema: the name of a
	// sunssf point, a literal exponent such as "-2", or empty for none.
	SFName string
	// SFRawValue is the resolved scale factor exponent, or nil when the point
	// has no scale factor or it could not be resolved (for example because
	// the device reports the sunssf point as not implemented).
	SFRawValue *int16
	// RegisterOffset is the offset of the point's first register from the
	// model's ID register, that is its index in DecodedModel.RawRegisters.
	RegisterOffset int
	// RegisterCount is the number of registers the point occupies.
	RegisterCount int
	// Implemented is false when the device reports the SunSpec "not
	// implemented" value for the point's type (for example 0x8000 for int16,
	// 0xFFFF for uint16, 0 for accumulators, NaN for floats, all NUL for
	// strings, the all-zero address for ipaddr and ipv6addr, and
	// FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF for eui48). RawValue then
	// holds that sentinel and must not be used as a measurement.
	Implemented bool
	// Symbols holds the names of the active symbols: at most one for an enum
	// whose value is listed in the schema, one per set bit that the schema
	// names for a bitfield. It is nil for other types.
	Symbols []string
}
```

DecodedPoint holds a single decoded point value.

#### func (DecodedPoint) MarshalJSON

```go
func (p DecodedPoint) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalJSON encodes the point with the same field names as the struct. JSON has no representation for NaN or infinity, so a float RawValue or a ScaledValue that is not a finite number is encoded as null. This is what a float point the device reports as not implemented looks like (Implemented is false and RawValue is NaN); without it, encoding a model with such a point fails.

#### func Detect

```go
func Detect(ctx context.Context, client *modbus.Client, opts *DiscoverOptions) (*DetectionResult, error)
```

Detect checks whether a device is SunSpec-enabled by probing each base address in opts (nil selects the defaults) for the "SunS" marker.

When at least one probe could be read but none held the marker, Detect returns a non-nil result with Detected false together with ErrNotSunSpec; the result's Attempts show what was read. When every probe failed, or opts is invalid, or ctx ended, it returns a nil result and the underlying error (for all-failed probes: the probe errors joined, so errors.Is matches each). A nil client is reported as an error wrapping modbus.ErrUnexpectedParameters.

Device holds a modbus client and discovery result, ready for reading.

The caller owns Client: Device does not open or close the connection. Concurrent Device use is safe to the same extent as the underlying client.

#### func Discover

```go
func Discover(ctx context.Context, client *modbus.Client, opts *DiscoverOptions) (*Device, error)
```

Discover detects SunSpec and enumerates models, returning a Device ready for reading.

It walks the model chain from the detected base address up to the end marker and attaches the registry schema to every model it knows. Models without a schema are kept, named "unknown\_\<ID>", and noted in Device.Discovery.Warnings; they can still be read as raw registers. A chain that is longer than opts.MaxModels is cut there without error; the missing end marker is noted in Device.Discovery.Warnings too.

Discover returns ErrNotSunSpec when no base address holds the marker, and otherwise the Modbus or chain error (ErrModelChainInvalid, ErrModelChainLimitExceeded) that stopped the walk; no partial Device is returned. A nil client is reported as an error wrapping modbus.ErrUnexpectedParameters. The returned Device uses opts.UnitID (1 when opts is nil or the unit ID is zero) and does not own client.

#### func NewDevice

```go
func NewDevice(client *modbus.Client, unitID uint8, discovery *DiscoveryResult) *Device
```

NewDevice creates a Device from an existing client and discovery result.

The Device reads with discovery.RegType. A nil discovery yields a Device without models that reads holding registers. NewDevice performs no I/O and does not take ownership of client.

#### func (Device) ModelByID

```go
func (d *Device) ModelByID(id uint16) *ModelInstance
```

ModelByID returns the first ModelInstance with the given model ID, or nil when the device does not expose that model.

The returned pointer refers to the element in d.Discovery.Models, so changes made through it are visible to later calls.

#### func (Device) ModelsByID

```go
func (d *Device) ModelsByID(id uint16) []ModelInstance
```

ModelsByID returns every instance of the given model ID, in chain order, or nil when the device does not expose that model. A device may expose a model more than once, for example one model 160 per MPPT tracker set.

The instances are copies: changing them does not change d.Discovery. Their Schema is still shared with the registry and must not be modified.

#### func (Device) ReadAll

```go
func (d *Device) ReadAll(ctx context.Context) ([]*DecodedModel, error)
```

ReadAll reads and decodes all discovered models with known schema. Unknown models are included with raw registers only.

ReadAll does not stop at the first failure: it returns one entry per discovered model, in discovery order, together with the first error it met. The entry of a model that failed carries the failure in its Warnings and whatever registers could be read. A Device without models returns nil, nil.

#### func (Device) ReadModel

```go
func (d *Device) ReadModel(ctx context.Context, inst ModelInstance) (*DecodedModel, error)
```

ReadModel reads and decodes a specific model instance.

It reads the model's two header registers at inst.Header.StartAddress and the inst.Header.Length data registers that follow, in as many Modbus requests as needed, and decodes them with inst.Schema. An instance without a schema yields a DecodedModel holding only RawRegisters and a warning, with a nil error.

The header registers are compared with inst.Header. A device that no longer reports that model ID and length at that address has changed its model chain since discovery (a firmware update, a reconfiguration, a different device behind the same address), and decoding its registers with the old layout would yield values that look valid and are not: ReadModel then returns an error matching ErrModelChanged. Discover again to continue.

On failure ReadModel returns a non-nil DecodedModel next to the error: for a read error it holds the data registers read so far (ErrPartialRead when a later chunk of a long model failed, otherwise the Modbus error as is); for a changed model it holds the data registers that were read, undecoded; for a device that reports fewer registers than the schema's fixed block needs it holds the raw registers and the error is a \*DecodeError.

#### func (Device) ReadModelByID

```go
func (d *Device) ReadModelByID(ctx context.Context, modelID uint16) (*DecodedModel, error)
```

ReadModelByID reads the first instance of the given model ID. It returns an error wrapping ErrUnknownModel when the device does not expose that model, and otherwise behaves like ReadModel.

#### func (Device) ReadModels

```go
func (d *Device) ReadModels(ctx context.Context, insts []ModelInstance) ([]ModelResult, error)
```

ReadModels reads and decodes the given instances, in fewer requests than ReadModel when they are adjacent in the model chain, as the instances of Discovery.Models are. It returns one ModelResult per instance, in input order. The error is nil when every instance succeeded; otherwise it wraps the first failure in input order, and each ModelResult carries its own. An empty insts returns nil, nil.

Adjacent instances share a request up to the Modbus limit of 125 registers; no register outside the instances is read. Every request includes the header of each instance it serves, which is checked as ReadModel checks it. An instance whose header and data fit in one request (Length of 123 or less) is never split, so its values and scale factors come from one response. A longer instance gets requests of its own and fails with ErrPartialRead, keeping the registers read, when one of them fails. An instance given twice is read once and decoded for each. The requests are made one after another; they are not an atomic snapshot of the device.

A Modbus exception fails only its request. When that request served several instances, as from a device that refuses reads across model boundaries, each of them is read again on its own, so every instance gets the result ReadModel would give it. A timeout or transport error ends the batch: the instances after it are not read. A cancelled or expired context ends it too.

ReadModels uses the function codes of ReadFunctionCodes only.

#### func (Device) ReadPoint

```go
func (d *Device) ReadPoint(ctx context.Context, inst ModelInstance, pointName string) (*DecodedPoint, error)
```

ReadPoint reads a single named point from a model instance.

The whole model is read and decoded, so the point's scale factor is resolved. The top-level group is searched first, then the nested group instances depth first in register order; the first point with a matching (case-sensitive) name wins, so for a point of a repeating group this is the one of the first instance. ReadPoint returns an error wrapping ErrPointNotFound when no decoded point has that name, which includes every point of a model without a schema, and the ReadModel error when the model cannot be read.

#### func (Device) WritePoint

```go
func (d *Device) WritePoint(ctx context.Context, inst ModelInstance, name string, value any) (*DecodedPoint, error)
```

WritePoint writes one top-level point of a model instance and returns the point as the device reports it afterwards.

It is the only method of this package that sends a write. It reads the model first, so that the header is checked (ErrModelChanged) and the point's scale factor is the device's current one, and encodes value as EncodeModel does: the engineering value for a scaled point, an enum symbol name, a list of bitfield symbol names, a string, or \[]uint16 with the point's exact registers. Then it writes the point's registers, and only those, with Write Multiple Registers (FC 16), and reads the model again.

A point that is not "RW" in the schema, a count point, a model without a schema and a Device on input registers fail with ErrPointNotWritable, and a name that is not a point of the top-level group with ErrPointNotFound, before anything is sent. A value the encoder refuses fails with its \*EncodeError. A device that refuses the write returns its Modbus exception (modbus.ErrIllegalDataAddress, say).

A client built with AllowedFunctionCodes: ReadFunctionCodes() cannot write: WritePoint then fails with modbus.ErrFunctionCodeNotAllowed.

### type DiscoverOptions

```go
type DiscoverOptions struct {
	// UnitID is the Modbus unit ID to address. Zero selects unit 1.
	UnitID uint8
	// RegType is the register type to probe and read. The zero value is
	// modbus.HoldingRegister, which is what nearly all SunSpec devices use.
	RegType modbus.RegType
	// BaseAddresses lists the register addresses probed for the "SunS"
	// marker, in order. Nil selects SunSpecDefaultBaseAddresses; an empty
	// non-nil slice is rejected.
	BaseAddresses []uint16
	// MaxModels caps the number of model headers read from the chain,
	// including the end marker. Zero or negative selects 256.
	MaxModels int
	// MaxAddressSpan caps how many registers past the base address the model
	// chain may extend; a longer chain fails with ErrModelChainLimitExceeded.
	// Zero disables the check.
	MaxAddressSpan uint16
}
```

DiscoverOptions configures detection and discovery. A nil \*DiscoverOptions selects the defaults described on each field.

### type DiscoveryResult

```go
type DiscoveryResult struct {
	// BaseAddress is the address of the "SunS" marker; the first model header
	// is at BaseAddress+2.
	BaseAddress uint16
	// RegType is the register type the marker was found in. Model data is
	// read with the same type.
	RegType modbus.RegType
	// Models lists the models in device order, without the end-of-chain
	// marker. It is empty for a device that exposes only the marker.
	Models []ModelInstance
	// Warnings holds human-readable notes, for example one entry per model
	// without a local schema.
	Warnings []string
	// Raw is the low-level discovery result, including the detection
	// attempts and the end-of-chain header. It is kept for debugging and may
	// be nil for a DiscoveryResult that was not produced by Discover.
	Raw *gmsunspec.DiscoveryResult
}
```

DiscoveryResult holds the enriched discovery output.

### type EncodeError

```go
type EncodeError struct {
	// ModelID is the model that failed to encode.
	ModelID uint16
	// Group is the path of the group instance the failure concerns, for
	// example "DERCurve/Crv[2]/Pt[1]": group names from the model's top-level
	// group down, with the 1-based instance number of each nested group. It
	// is empty when the failure concerns the model as a whole.
	Group string
	// PointName is the point that failed, or empty when the failure concerns
	// a group or the model.
	PointName string
	// PointType is the SunSpec type of the failing point, or empty.
	PointType string
	// Message describes the failure. When empty, Err's message is used.
	Message string
	// Err is the cause, for example ErrValueOutOfRange or ErrPointNotFound,
	// or nil when there is none more specific than ErrEncode.
	Err error
}
```

EncodeError describes why values could not be encoded into a model, with the location of the failure. errors.Is matches it against ErrEncode and against its cause.

#### func (EncodeError) Error

```go
func (e *EncodeError) Error() string
```

Error formats the failure as "sunspec: encode model \<id> \[group \<path>] \[point \<name>] \[type \<t>]: \<message>". A nil \*EncodeError formats as a generic encode error.

#### func (EncodeError) Is

```go
func (e *EncodeError) Is(target error) bool
```

Is reports whether target is ErrEncode, so that errors.Is(err, ErrEncode) holds for every EncodeError whatever its cause.

#### func (EncodeError) Unwrap

```go
func (e *EncodeError) Unwrap() error
```

Unwrap returns the cause, which may be nil. A nil \*EncodeError unwraps to nil.

### type ModelHeader

```go
type ModelHeader struct {
	// ID is the SunSpec model ID read from the device (for example 1 for
	// Common, 101 for a single phase inverter).
	ID uint16
	// Length is the number of data registers that follow the two-register
	// model header (ID and L), as reported by the device.
	Length uint16
	// StartAddress is the address of the model header, i.e. of the ID
	// register. The model data starts at StartAddress+2.
	StartAddress uint16
	// EndAddress is the address of the last register of the model
	// (StartAddress+1+Length).
	EndAddress uint16
	// NextAddress is the address of the header of the model that follows
	// (EndAddress+1).
	NextAddress uint16
	// IsEndModel reports whether this is the end-of-chain marker (ID 0xFFFF,
	// length 0). Discover never returns such a header in DiscoveryResult.Models.
	IsEndModel bool
}
```

ModelHeader describes where one SunSpec model sits in the device's register map. All addresses are zero-based Modbus register addresses.

### type ModelInstance

```go
type ModelInstance struct {
	// Header locates the model in the device's register map.
	Header ModelHeader
	// Name is the schema label, or the schema name when the label is empty,
	// or "unknown_<ID>" when the registry has no schema for the model ID.
	Name string
	// Schema is the compiled schema for Header.ID, or nil when SchemaKnown is
	// false. It is shared with the registry and must not be modified.
	Schema *registry.ModelMeta
	// SchemaKnown reports whether the registry has a schema for Header.ID.
	SchemaKnown bool
	// DecodingSupported reports whether Device.ReadModel decodes this model
	// into points. Models without it are returned as raw registers only.
	DecodingSupported bool
}
```

ModelInstance represents one discovered model instance enriched with schema metadata.

### type ModelResult

```go
type ModelResult struct {
	// Instance is the instance as given to ReadModels.
	Instance ModelInstance
	// Model is what ReadModel returns for the instance, partial registers
	// included. It is nil when the instance was not read because the batch
	// stopped before it.
	Model *DecodedModel
	// Err is the instance's error as ReadModel returns it (ErrModelChanged,
	// ErrPartialRead, a *DecodeError, a Modbus error), or one wrapping
	// batch.ErrNotAttempted and the reason the batch stopped. Nil on success.
	Err error
}
```

ModelResult is the outcome of reading one model instance with ReadModels.

### type ProbeAttempt

```go
type ProbeAttempt struct {
	// BaseAddress is the register address that was probed for the marker.
	BaseAddress uint16
	// RegType is the register type that was read.
	RegType modbus.RegType
	// Registers holds the two registers read at BaseAddress, or nil when the
	// read failed or returned a short response.
	Registers []uint16
	// Matched reports whether Registers holds the "SunS" marker.
	Matched bool
	// Error is the read error for this probe, or nil. It is not marshalled to
	// JSON; use ErrorString for that.
	Error error `json:"-"`
	// ErrorString is Error.Error(), or empty when the probe did not fail.
	ErrorString string `json:"error,omitempty"`
}
```

ProbeAttempt holds one base-address probe during SunSpec detection.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// image holds the device map from the marker to the end marker;
	// image[0] is the register at base.

}
```

Server is a SunSpec device held in memory and served over Modbus: the "SunS" marker at the base address, then each model (ID and length registers, data), then the end marker.

A Server is a go-modbus RequestHandler. It does not listen itself: pass it to modbus.NewServer, which owns the listener, the connections, logging, metrics and TLS, or call Serve for the common case.

	srv, err := sunspec.NewServer(&sunspec.ServerOptions{BaseAddress: 40000}, models...)
	ms, err := modbus.NewServer(&modbus.ServerConfig{URL: "tcp://0.0.0.0:1502"}, srv)
	err = ms.Start()

#### Requests {#hdr-Requests}

Reads of the configured register type are answered for any range inside the device map, also one that spans several models. A range that touches an address outside the map is answered with exception 2 (illegal data address), as is any request for the other register type. A request for another unit ID is answered with exception 0x0B (gateway target device failed to respond), or not at all with ServerOptions.SilentToOtherUnits. A request for unit ID 0, the Modbus broadcast address, is never answered and never carried out. Coils and discrete inputs do not exist: exception 1 (illegal function).

#### Writes {#hdr-Writes}

A client may write (function codes 6 and 16) the points whose schema access is "RW", in a model served from values. A write must cover whole points and nothing else. Writing anything else is refused with exception 2 and changes nothing: read-only points, the marker, the ID and length registers, the count point of a group, part of a multi-register point, a model served from raw registers, an address outside the map. The Server stores the registers of an accepted write as they are; it does not judge values. Give an OnWrite function to validate, refuse or observe writes. Function codes 22 (mask write) and 23 (read/write) are not supported.

#### Updates and concurrency {#hdr-Updates_and_concurrency}

All methods are safe for concurrent use with each other and with requests being served. Each update (SetPoint, SetValues, Update, SetRegisters) and each accepted client write replaces a model's registers atomically: a single Modbus read never sees half of it. A client that needs several requests for one model (more than 125 registers) can see different updates in different requests, as with any Modbus device.

The layout is fixed when the Server is created. An update cannot change the length of a model.

#### func NewServer

```go
func NewServer(opts *ServerOptions, models ...ServerModel) (*Server, error)
```

NewServer lays out a device from the given models, in order.

It returns the error of EncodeModel for a model whose values cannot be encoded, an error matching ErrUnknownModel for a model given without registers whose ID has no schema in the registry, and an error matching ErrModelLayout when a model has no data registers, uses the end marker's ID 65535, is longer than 65535 registers, or the chain does not fit between the base address and address 65535. A device without models is valid: it serves the marker and the end marker.

The models' values and registers are copied.

#### func (Server) BaseAddress

```go
func (s *Server) BaseAddress() uint16
```

BaseAddress returns the register address of the "SunS" marker.

#### func (Server) HandleCoils

```go
func (s *Server) HandleCoils(_ context.Context, _ *modbus.CoilsRequest) ([]bool, error)
```

HandleCoils rejects every coil request with modbus.ErrIllegalFunction: a SunSpec device map has no coils.

#### func (Server) HandleDiscreteInputs

```go
func (s *Server) HandleDiscreteInputs(_ context.Context, _ *modbus.DiscreteInputsRequest) ([]bool, error)
```

HandleDiscreteInputs rejects every discrete input request with modbus.ErrIllegalFunction.

#### func (Server) HandleHoldingRegisters

```go
func (s *Server) HandleHoldingRegisters(ctx context.Context, req *modbus.HoldingRegistersRequest) ([]uint16, error)
```

HandleHoldingRegisters serves reads and writes of holding registers as described on Server. A nil request is answered with modbus.ErrServerDeviceFailure.

#### func (Server) HandleInputRegisters

```go
func (s *Server) HandleInputRegisters(_ context.Context, req *modbus.InputRegistersRequest) ([]uint16, error)
```

HandleInputRegisters serves reads of input registers when the Server was created with RegType modbus.InputRegister; otherwise every address is answered with modbus.ErrIllegalDataAddress. A nil request is answered with modbus.ErrServerDeviceFailure.

#### func (Server) Model

```go
func (s *Server) Model(index int) (*DecodedModel, error)
```

Model returns the model at index of the chain as it is served right now, decoded the way a client reads it; client writes that were accepted are visible in it. The result is a snapshot that the caller owns.

A model served from raw registers yields a DecodedModel holding only the data registers in RawRegisters and a warning, as Device.ReadModel does for a model without schema. Model returns an error matching ErrUnknownModel for an index outside the chain.

#### func (Server) Models

```go
func (s *Server) Models() []ModelHeader
```

Models returns where each model sits in the device map, in chain order, without the end marker: what a client's discovery finds. The position of a model in the result is the index the other methods take.

#### func (Server) RegType

```go
func (s *Server) RegType() modbus.RegType
```

RegType returns the register type the device map is served in.

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(ctx context.Context, conf *modbus.ServerConfig) error
```

Serve listens as conf says and serves the device until ctx is done, then shuts the listener and its connections down and returns nil. It is a convenience for

	ms, err := modbus.NewServer(conf, s)
	err = ms.Start()
	<-ctx.Done()
	err = ms.Shutdown(...)

and the one place where this package opens a listener; use those calls directly to control the lifecycle yourself. conf.URL selects the transport (go-modbus serves "tcp://host:port" and "tcp+tls://host:port"); conf also carries the idle timeout, client limit, TLS material, logger and metrics.

Serve returns the go-modbus error when conf is invalid or the address cannot be listened on, and the shutdown error when connections do not end within five seconds.

#### func (Server) SetPoint

```go
func (s *Server) SetPoint(index int, name string, value any) error
```

SetPoint sets one point of the top-level group of the model at index of the chain, leaving every other value as it is. A nil value makes the point not implemented. Use Update to change points of nested groups or several points at once. It returns the errors of Update.

#### func (Server) SetRegisters

```go
func (s *Server) SetRegisters(index int, data []uint16) error
```

SetRegisters replaces the data registers (what follows the ID and length registers) of the model at index of the chain. It works for every model. For a model served from values, those values are replaced by what the new registers decode to, and the registers must describe the same group structure as before: the same counts, nothing left over.

Nothing changes when SetRegisters returns an error: one matching ErrModelLayout when len(data) is not the model's length or the registers would change the group structure, or ErrUnknownModel for an index outside the chain. data is copied.

#### func (Server) SetValues

```go
func (s *Server) SetValues(index int, values *Values) error
```

SetValues replaces all values of the model at index of the chain: points that values does not hold become not implemented. It is Update with a function that discards the current values, and returns the same errors. values is copied.

#### func (Server) UnitID

```go
func (s *Server) UnitID() uint8
```

UnitID returns the Modbus unit ID the device answers.

#### func (Server) Update

```go
func (s *Server) Update(index int, fn func(v *Values) error) error
```

Update changes the values of the model at index of the chain in one atomic step. fn receives a copy of the model's current values, including what clients wrote, and modifies it; when fn returns nil the model is encoded from the result and replaces the served registers.

Nothing changes when Update returns an error: the error fn returned, the error of EncodeModel for values that cannot be encoded, an error matching ErrModelLayout when the new values would change the model's length (a different number of group instances), ErrUnknownModel for an index outside the chain, or ErrEncode for a model served from raw registers (use SetRegisters).

fn runs while the Server is locked: it must not call methods of the Server.

### type ServerModel

```go
type ServerModel struct {
	// ID is the SunSpec model ID. It may be left zero when Schema is set.
	ID uint16
	// Schema is the schema the values are encoded with. Nil selects the
	// registry's schema for ID. It is ignored when Registers is set.
	Schema *registry.ModelMeta
	// Values holds the point values, see Values. Nil serves the model with
	// every point not implemented. It must be nil when Registers is set.
	Values *Values
	// Registers holds the model's data registers: what follows the ID and
	// length registers. When it is not nil the model is served from these
	// registers as they are, its length is len(Registers), and no schema is
	// applied. It must not be empty.
	Registers []uint16
}
```

ServerModel defines one model of a served device.

A model is given either by values, which are encoded with a schema, or by its data registers. The first form supports updates by point name and client writes; the second serves any model, including vendor models the registry does not know, as an opaque read-only block.

### type ServerOptions

```go
type ServerOptions struct {
	// UnitID is the only Modbus unit ID the device answers. Zero selects
	// unit 1, as in DiscoverOptions.
	UnitID uint8
	// SilentToOtherUnits makes the device ignore requests for another unit
	// ID, the way a device on a serial line does: the client gets no answer
	// and runs into its timeout. By default such a request is answered with
	// exception 0x0B (gateway target device failed to respond), which tells
	// a client at once that the unit is not there. Added in v0.5.1.
	SilentToOtherUnits bool
	// BaseAddress is the register address of the "SunS" marker. The zero
	// value is address 0, one of the standard SunSpec base addresses; most
	// devices use 40000. A client only finds the device at an address it
	// probes (SunSpecDefaultBaseAddresses for this package's Discover).
	BaseAddress uint16
	// RegType is the register type the device map is served in. The zero
	// value is modbus.HoldingRegister, which is what nearly all SunSpec
	// devices use. With modbus.InputRegister the map is read-only: Modbus
	// has no function to write input registers.
	RegType modbus.RegType
	// OnWrite, when not nil, is called for every client write that passed
	// the Server's own checks, before it takes effect. Returning nil accepts
	// the write. Returning an error rejects it: nothing changes and the
	// client receives that error as a Modbus exception (return
	// modbus.ErrIllegalDataValue to refuse a value; an error that is not a
	// Modbus exception is reported as a server device failure).
	//
	// OnWrite runs while the Server is locked, so that the write is atomic.
	// It must not call methods of the Server and should return quickly.
	OnWrite func(ctx context.Context, w *ServerWrite) error
}
```

ServerOptions configures a Server. A nil \*ServerOptions selects unit ID 1, base address 0 and holding registers.

### type ServerWrite

```go
type ServerWrite struct {
	// ClientAddr is the address of the client, as reported by go-modbus.
	ClientAddr string
	// ModelIndex is the position of the written model in the device's chain,
	// starting at 0.
	ModelIndex int
	// ModelID is the SunSpec ID of the written model.
	ModelID uint16
	// Address is the address of the first register written.
	Address uint16
	// Registers holds the register values written.
	Registers []uint16
	// Points holds the points covered by the write, in register order,
	// decoded as they will be once the write is accepted. RegisterOffset
	// tells instances of a repeating group apart.
	Points []DecodedPoint
	// Model is the whole model as it will be once the write is accepted.
	Model *DecodedModel
}
```

ServerWrite describes a client write to a served device, as passed to ServerOptions.OnWrite.

### type Values

```go
type Values struct {
	// Points maps a point name of the group to its value.
	Points map[string]any
	// Groups maps the name of a nested group to its instances.
	Groups map[string][]*Values
}
```

Values holds the values of one group instance of a model: the group's own points by name and the instances of the groups nested inside it. It is the input of EncodeModel and of the Server, and the write-side counterpart of DecodedGroup.

A point that is absent from Points, or whose value is nil, is encoded as the SunSpec "not implemented" value of its type. The value of a present point may be:

  - any Go integer or float type, or a json.Number, for a numeric point (int16 … uint64, acc16 … acc64, count, sunssf, enum, bitfield, pad, float32, float64). For a point with a scale factor this is the engineering value, see below.
  - a string for a string, ipaddr ("192.168.1.10"), ipv6addr ("fe80::1") or eui48 ("00:11:22:33:44:55") point.
  - a string naming one of the schema's symbols for an enum16 or enum32 point, and a \[]string naming the bits to set for a bitfield point.
  - a \[]uint16 with exactly as many elements as the point has registers, for any point: the registers are used as they are.

#### Scale factors {#hdr-Scale_factors}

A point whose schema names a scale factor takes the engineering value: the encoder divides it by 10^sf and stores the nearest integer, halves rounded away from zero. The scale factor is the value given for the sunssf point of that name in the same Values or, failing that, in an enclosing one (or the literal exponent of the schema). So {"W": 1234.5, "W\_SF": -1} stores 12345 in W. When the sunssf point is not set at any level the value is stored unscaled, which is how DecodeModel reads such a point. Unscaled integer points round a fractional value the same way.

A value that does not fit the point's type after scaling, or that would collide with the type's "not implemented" value (for example 65535 for a uint16), is rejected with an error matching ErrValueOutOfRange; nothing is wrapped or clamped. Accumulators accept 0 although it reads back as not implemented.

#### Groups {#hdr-Groups}

Groups maps the name of a nested group to its instances in register order. The number of instances that is encoded follows the schema (registry.GroupMeta):

  - CountPoint set: the value given for that count point, or, when the count point is not set, the largest number of instances given for any group that is counted by it. The count point itself is encoded with that number, so an unset count point reads back as that number, not as "not implemented". Groups with fewer instances are completed with instances whose points are all not implemented; more instances than an explicit count is an error.
  - Count > 0: exactly that many, completed the same way.
  - Count == 0: as many as given.

A nil \*Values, as a model's values or as an instance, is an instance without any value.

#### func (Values) Add

```go
func (v *Values) Add(group string, inst *Values) *Values
```

Add appends one instance of the named nested group and returns that instance. A nil inst adds an empty instance.

#### func (Values) Clone

```go
func (v *Values) Clone() *Values
```

Clone returns a deep copy of v: maps, instances and slice values are copied. A nil v yields nil.

#### func (Values) Set

```go
func (v *Values) Set(name string, value any) *Values
```

Set stores value for the named point and returns v, so that calls can be chained. It allocates Points when needed.
